Subject: SDK integration: temporary exemption request & roadmap clarification

Team — quick summary from Acme POC (Sara): since last week they started seeing intermittent stream truncation and 5xxs when long-running streaming conversations (avg 8–12k tokens) with prefetch enabled are used alongside our SDK session migration. They reproduce it predictably when a heavy prefetch + multiplex background job hits while the session is being migrated across hosts.

Impact: demo environment (staging) fails ~1/20 sessions; production POC saw 3 customer-critical demo failures across two accounts. Acme is asking for a short-term workaround routing them to a stable runtime variant while we put a permanent fix on the roadmap. They are sensitive to latency increases, so any workaround must keep p50 under 120ms.

What I need from Platform/Product: 
- Can we provision an exemption to route Acme traffic to the "stable-prefetch-off" runtime variant for 30 days?
- Is there an SDK-level toggle or header that we can expose quickly so they can opt out of client prefetch behavior while keeping other benefits?
- If not exposed, can platform accept an opt-in header today (internal-only) to force session stickiness?

Attachments: acme_logs_1128.zip (traces + minimal repro steps), session_trace_1128.txt
Proposed next step: short mutual action plan (link below) and a temporary routing exemption while we scope a proper runtime fix.

Thanks — Rafael

Thanks for the data and the traces — I dug into the session traces in acme_logs_1128.zip. Quick technical read: we are seeing a race between the prefetch KV warm path and the session migration handshake. When the client triggers prefetch immediately before the migration completes, the small window causes duplicate session initialization on the new host and stale KV pointers; the runtime then returns a state mismatch which surfaces as a 5xx or truncated stream in the client.

Mitigations (short/medium term):
- Immediate temporary: add an opt-in internal header X-RI-SESSION-STICKY: 1 that forces the router to pin the session to the current host until we confirm the KV cache exchange. This is internal-only but can be configured per-tenant.
- Client-side mitigation (can be shipped quickly): SDK exposes a config prefetch.enabled = false or prefetch.delay_ms = 2500 to avoid triggering prefetch during migration windows. We can ship an SDK patch that surfaces this config as an application-level option (opt-in) within 48–72 hours.
- Long-term fix: make KV fetch idempotent and delay prefetch until post-migration commit; this requires runtime work and QA (~4–6 sprints).

I can provision the temporary per-tenant routing flag for Acme if Product approves and Infra will accept the exception. I attached temp_prefetch_patch.diff to show a minimal server-side check.

Questions for Product: are we comfortable exposing prefetch.disable as a documented SDK toggle (opt-in) to customers? That reduces our automatic optimizations but gives field safety. If not, we should allow the internal header and a documented rollback path.

— Karthik

Thanks for the analysis Karthik — that matches product's instincts. A few notes from roadmap/PM: 
- We are open to exposing an "escape hatch" in the SDK as an opt-in customer config (prefetch.disable or prefetch.delay_ms). We need a small RFC and QA matrix (compat with streaming + embeddings + function calling).
- We should avoid making this the default behavior; the product tradeoff is reduced cold-start quality for customers who keep prefetch off. The header X-RI-SESSION-STICKY as an internal, per-tenant flag is acceptable as a short-term exception.
- Timeline: if Platform can provide the internal header and Infra will permit a tenant-level rule, Product can greenlight an SDK opt-in toggle in the next release (target 2 weeks) assuming QA passes. Long-term runtime fix stays on the 4–6 sprint horizon.

Marissa/Rafael — please compile a short customer impact summary (customers affected, repro frequency, tolerance for latency bump) and I'm happy to fast-track the RFC. Jonas — can you own the infra policy to gate tenant exceptions?

— Tessa Morgan
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

1) Platform: please provision per-tenant header support for X-RI-SESSION-STICKY: 1 and enable it for Acme's tenant ID (ACME-tenant-71) as a 30-day exception. Karthik, confirm ETA for the toggle and any rollback steps.

2) SDK: Marissa / SDK team to ship an opt-in config prefetch.disable (or prefetch.delay_ms) in the next minor release. Marissa — can we have a test build by Dec 4 so Acme can validate in staging?

3) Product: Tessa to fast-track RFC and QA sign-off once we have the customer impact summary (I'll paste the repro frequency below).

Customer impact (from Sara): staging repro ~1/20 sessions; production POC saw 3 demo failures across a week. Acme can tolerate up to +25ms p50 but not >120ms. They prefer the SDK opt-in rather than a long-term routing move but will accept routing as an interim if shipping the SDK change will take >1 week.

Attachments: acme_mutual_action_plan_20291202.xlsx (short MAP we reviewed with Sara), session_trace_1128.txt, temp_prefetch_patch.diff

Marissa — can you coordinate with Acme to accept the 30-day exemption and confirm they will run the staging validation once they get the test build? I'll update the HubSpot record and push the MAP link to procurement.
